newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh-Iranian oil swap stalled by quality problem.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh-Iranian oil swap stalled by quality problem.

text.p: An oil swaps deal between Kazakhstan and Iran has been stalled by a dispute over crude quality, a senior Kazakh official said on Monday.

Deputy Oil and Gas Minister Anatoly Lobayev, quoted by Interfax news agency, said that Kazakh and Iranian officials failed during a recent meeting in Tehran to agree on issues pertaining to the quality of Kazakh oil to be delivered by tankers to northern Iran across the Caspian Sea.
The oil and gas ministry was disbanded recently and replaced by a new state-owned company called Kazakh Oil.
Lobayev said the main stumbling block was the high concentration of mercaptans in Kazakh oil. Mercaptans are undesirable, foul-smelling sulphur compounds.
Trial shipments of Kazakh oil across the Caspian Sea to an Iranian port -- targeted at two million tonnes a year -- began in January.
But Lobayev said Kazakh oil shipments to Iran reached only 70,000 this year and were suspended because of the mercaptans problem.

"To do away with these admixtures completely, as Iran insists, it is necessary to build an oil refinery of our own," Lobayev said, adding that the Kazakh side was providing a "sufficient degree of refining".

Under the swaps deal, agreed last year, Iran would initially refine 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Kazakh crude blended with its own Iran Light crude. After two years the amount would increase to 120,000 bpd.

In return, land-locked Kazakhstan, which has traditionally relied on neighbouring Russia's pipelines to export output, would be entitled to the same value of crude oil at Iranian export terminals in the Persian Gulf or at Iran's storage facilities in Europe.
